You are an evidence extractor for an equity research desk. You read ONE news item and turn what it says into structured evidence cards. You only report what the text itself says. You do not use outside knowledge, you do not guess what happened later, and you do not forecast prices.

WATCHED COMPANIES (use exactly these tickers):
- NVDA: NVIDIA, Nvidia
- AAPL: Apple
- GOOGL: Alphabet, Google, GOOG
- META: Meta Platforms, Meta, Facebook
- AMZN: Amazon, AWS
- TSLA: Tesla
- MSTR: MicroStrategy, Strategy Inc
- COIN: Coinbase
- HOOD: Robinhood
- CRCL: Circle Internet, Circle

A text may name a company by its ticker, by its company name, or via a product ticker such as "2x Long NVDA ETF" (that counts as NVDA). Leveraged/inverse ETFs on a company count as that company. Companies not in the list above never get a name card.

CARD TYPES
- scope "name": the text says something specific about a watched company (its business, results, products, deals, guidance, analyst actions, regulation, management, or its own stock). One card per watched company, "tickers" = [that ticker]. A company that only appears in a list of movers or a passing mention with no information about it gets NO card.
- scope "sector": the text says something about an industry or theme but not about a specific watched company. "tickers" = [] and "sector" = one of: ai_semis, megacap_tech, crypto, fintech, ev_auto, other. At most 2 sector cards.
- scope "market": the text says something about the overall US stock market or risk appetite (Fed and rates, inflation data, geopolitics, index moves, broad flows). "tickers" = [] and "sector" = "". At most 1 market card.
If the text says nothing relevant to US equities, crypto or macro risk appetite, return {"cards": []}.

NO CARD for a watched company when it only appears:
- in a list of tickers, price changes, fund flows, positions or "representative stocks" where it gets a number or a few words and no reason specific to it;
- in advertisements, promotions, giveaways, disclaimers or navigation text;
- as a benchmark, comparison or background name in an article about another company.
Exception: if an article about another company states a concrete fact that directly affects the watched company (it signs a deal with it, becomes its customer or tenant, wins or loses business from it), give a name card with strength at most 0.4.

FIELDS (per card)
- stance: integer -2..2. The direction the reported information points for that company / sector / market. +2 clearly and strongly positive (e.g. large earnings beat with raised guidance, major contract, upgrade with a big target raise); +1 positive; 0 neutral, mixed or purely descriptive; -1 negative; -2 clearly and strongly negative. Judge the information, not the tone of the headline.
- strength: number 0..1. How material, specific and well-supported the information is for that subject. 0.1 = vague or passing; 0.4 = clear but modest; 0.7 = specific and material; 0.9 = major, confirmed, company-specific.
- horizon_h: integer hours the information is likely to stay relevant: 4-24 for intraday flow or sentiment; 24-72 for ordinary news; 72-240 for earnings, guidance, analyst actions, deals; up to 720 for structural changes.
- novelty: "new" if the text reports a development for the first time (an announcement, data release, deal, filing, analyst action, product news). "recap" if it summarises developments that are already known: weekly or daily roundups, previews of upcoming events, general outlook or opinion pieces. "post_hoc" if the text explains why a price ALREADY moved: titles or texts like "[Market Movement Analysis]", "[Market Movement Interpretation]", "X surges on <date>: ...", "why X stock fell today". Decide novelty per card: a card whose content is mainly that the stock or market already rose or fell (with or without reasons) is "post_hoc", even inside a daily roundup. A post_hoc card still gets the stance of the reasons it gives.
- summary: one English sentence, at most 200 characters, stating the information for that subject.
- quote: one contiguous verbatim excerpt (at most 25 words) copied from the text that supports the card. Copy it exactly: no paraphrase, no ellipses, no joining of separate sentences.

OUTPUT
Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"cards": [{"scope": "name|sector|market", "tickers": ["NVDA"], "sector": "", "stance": 1, "strength": 0.6, "horizon_h": 72, "novelty": "new", "summary": "...", "quote": "..."}]}

TITLE: Bitget UEX Daily | PCE Comes in Below Expectations; Tech Stocks Rebound; HPE Wins $1.2 Billion AI Order (September 30)

TEXT:
I. Hot News Highlights
Federal Reserve & Inflation
Softer PCE eases immediate tightening pressure
August headline PCE inflation was 0.3% month over month and 3.4% year over year. Core PCE rose 0.2% monthly and 3.0% annually. Methodology changes and historical revisions also affected the release.
Market Impact: The softer reading supports risk appetite, but slower tightening is not the same as the start of an easing cycle. Energy prices and subsequent employment data remain important.
US Economy
GDP revised higher; private employment continues growing
Second-quarter real GDP growth was revised to an annualized 2.2%. September ADP private employment increased by 90,000, following a revised 36,000 gain in August.
Market Impact: Resilient growth reduces immediate recession concerns but may keep longer-term financing costs elevated. Earnings growth must offset that pressure to sustain equity valuations.
International Commodities
Oil rebounds; Brent contract rollover requires care
WTI settled at $90.42 per barrel, up 1.2%. Expiring November Brent settled at $103.50, up 0.9%; the more active December contract was quoted at $98.03, up 1.9%.
Market Impact: Higher energy costs could offset some inflation relief. The gap between November and December Brent means a rollover-related price change should not be mistaken for a sudden market selloff.
II. Market Review
Commodities & Forex
Spot gold was $4,152.86 per ounce, down 0.7%, at approximately 13:40 Eastern time. Spot silver was $60.18, down 2.1%. WTI settled at $90.42, while December Brent was quoted at $98.03. The Dollar Index was 101.20, down 0.20%, in the verified report.
Driver Analysis: Softer inflation did not produce a uniform rally. Energy costs and long-term rate pressure remain constraints on precious metals and other rate-sensitive assets.
Cryptocurrency Performance
BTC traded at approximately 83,618.47 USDT, up 0.05% over a rolling 24 hours, with approximately $240.81 million in Bitget pair turnover. ETH traded at approximately 2,671.72 USDT, down 0.72%, with approximately $131.26 million in pair turnover. These volumes represent the corresponding Bitget spot pairs, not the entire market.
CoinGecko showed total cryptocurrency market capitalization of approximately $2.97 trillion and market-wide 24-hour turnover of approximately $100.7 billion.
Large-Holder Positioning: Strategy purchased 1,665 BTC during September 21–27 for approximately $142.7 million, averaging $85,681. Total holdings reached 847,666 BTC, with an aggregate average cost of $75,437. BitMine added 17,362 ETH in its latest week, reaching 6,001,302 ETH, including 5,067,309 staked. These September 28 disclosures are weekly figures, not purchases made today.
Price–Volume Analysis: BTC was broadly flat while ETH declined, so the snapshot does not show a synchronized breakout. Corporate treasury purchases demonstrate continuing allocation demand, but trading volume alone cannot establish whale accumulation. Confirmation requires successive volume observations, ETF flows and updated holdings disclosures.

Performance Summary: Five advanced and two declined. Alphabet led, while Meta retreated. The rebound reflects improved market conditions, not proof of simultaneous fundamental improvement across every AI-related company.
Sector Observation
AI servers and networking: HPE ’s Vultr order and higher networking targets provide additional demand evidence. Delivery, margins and collections will determine the earnings contribution.
Chip-design software: Synopsys and OpenAI announced GPT - Synopsys , combining a specialized model with EDA tools. Adoption, verification reliability and incremental revenue are the next tests.
III. Featured US Equity Analysis
1. HPE (HPE) — Order execution follows stronger growth targets
Event Overview: HPE announced a $1.2 billion Vultr order for AMD Helios systems and raised its fiscal 2027 networking revenue growth outlook to the high teens–low twenties.
Market Interpretation: Integrating compute, networking and cooling expands HPE’s role in AI projects. Order value, however, is not immediate revenue or profit.
What to Watch: Deployment schedules, networking margins, order conversion and working-capital requirements.
2. Synopsys ( SNPS ) — Specialized AI enters engineering workflows
Event Overview: Synopsys and OpenAI agreed to develop GPT-Synopsys with revenue sharing. Synopsys also announced a multiyear Amazon collaboration covering chip IP , cloud and AI engineering.
Market Interpretation: Better engineering productivity could increase software value, but technical demonstrations do not establish production reliability or immediate financial returns.
What to Watch: Customer deployments, pricing, verified design outcomes and incremental revenue.
3. Micron ( MU ) — Earnings must validate memory demand
Event Overview: Micron scheduled its fourth-quarter earnings call for September 30 at 14:30 Mountain time, equivalent to October 1 at 04:30 Beijing time. Unverified earnings figures are not included here.
Market Interpretation: The key question is how HBM, DRAM and NAND demand translates into revenue, margins and cash generation.
What to Watch: Forward guidance, HBM deliveries, capacity ramp-up, capital spending and free cash flow.
IV. Market & Project Updates
1. Strategy continues BTC accumulation. Its latest weekly purchase lifted holdings to 847,666 BTC.
2. BitMine exceeds 6 million ETH. Approximately 5.07 million ETH are staked, making staking income another factor alongside token prices.
3. Synopsys and OpenAI pursue specialized AI. The collaboration targets chip-design workflows and joint commercialization.
4. HPE wins an AI infrastructure order. Vultr’s $1.2 billion order uses AMD Helios systems.
